title: Pre-scrolling the grouped window tool tip to the final entry leaves part of the delegate out of view
line: The grouped window tooltip now opens scrolled to the active window on multi-screen setups, even the first time it is shown.
explanation: The grouped tooltip's maximumWidth was Screen.desktopAvailableWidth, the width of the whole desktop across all screens, and maximumHeight used that same width by mistake. With more than one screen the list was first laid out at that provisional size (2296 px instead of 1016 px on the rig) and positioned at the active window, then the tooltip was shrunk to fit its screen without re-positioning, so the active window ended up partly or fully out of view; vertical panels hit the same through the height. Later shows reuse the final size, which is why it only happens sometimes. The maximum width and height now come from the tooltip's own screen (Screen.width/Screen.height), so the list is laid out at its final size from the start.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: limit grouped tooltip to its own screen size

The grouped tooltip's maximum size used the width of the whole desktop,
so with several screens it was first laid out too wide, then shrunk to
the screen, leaving the active window out of view. Use the screen size.

BUG: 522287

Subject: [PATCH] applets/taskmanager: limit grouped tooltip to its own screen
 size

The grouped tooltip's maximum size used the width of the whole desktop,
so with several screens it was first laid out too wide, then shrunk to
the screen, leaving the active window out of view. Use the screen size.

BUG: 522287

diff --git a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
index 014e954c5c..11ba6bf553 100644
--- a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
+++ b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
@@ -91,8 +91,8 @@ Loader {
         PlasmaComponents3.ScrollView {
             id: scrollView
             // 2 * Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing is for the margin of tooltipDialog
-            readonly property real maximumWidth: Screen.desktopAvailableWidth - 2 * Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing
-            readonly property real maximumHeight: Screen.desktopAvailableWidth - 2 * Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing
+            readonly property real maximumWidth: Screen.width - 2 * Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing
+            readonly property real maximumHeight: Screen.height - 2 * Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing
 
             implicitWidth: {
                 // when vertical, all delegates have the same fixed width, but with an extra

review.text: Replacing Screen.desktopAvailableWidth (which spanned the entire virtual desktop across all monitors and was also mistakenly used for maximumHeight) with Screen.width and Screen.height fixes the real root cause of grouped tooltips being laid out too large and shrunk after positionViewAtIndex(). The 2-line fix matches GroupDialog.qml, has no workarounds or side effects, and is well verified across multi-screen, single-screen, horizontal, and vertical panels.

reviews.text: Replacing Screen.desktopAvailableWidth (which spanned the entire virtual desktop across all monitors and was also mistakenly used for maximumHeight) with Screen.width and Screen.height fixes the real root cause of grouped tooltips being laid out too large and shrunk after positionViewAtIndex(). The 2-line fix matches GroupDialog.qml, has no workarounds or side effects, and is well verified across multi-screen, single-screen, horizontal, and vertical panels.

The change is a real fix: maximumWidth used the whole multi-screen desktop width and maximumHeight used a width by mistake, and the logs (2296 px laid out, then shrunk to 1016) plus the two-screen before/after shots show that this breaks the first pre-scroll on multi-screen setups. But the reporter is on a single laptop screen with no mention of a second monitor, and on a single screen this patch changes nothing for a horizontal panel. The 2026-11-19 sweep test (kdetest3, default single output, scale 1.25) saw the tooltip open at Image 01-04 in 2 of 3 fresh tries, while this fix's single-screen check saw master right 2/2. Since the bug is timing-dependent, two tries can't rule out a remaining single-screen cause, so it isn't shown that the reporter's case is closed.
changes: Repeat the single-output scale-1.25 setup from the sweep test (15 windows, fresh plasmashell, first hover) on master and with the fix, enough runs to compare; if master still fails there, find and fix that cause too (e.g. re-run positionViewAtIndex once the list's final width is set) before using BUG:
Also test the panel on a non-primary screen of a different logical size, since Screen.* on a tooltip window that isn't mapped yet can report the primary screen during the first layout
If single-screen truly can't reproduce, say so in the commit/notes and check with the reporter whether they use more than one monitor
